policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV explicitly renders the qere as a destination noun in ‘put him into prison,’ distinguishing הַכְּלוּא from the ketiv הכליא.
ASV ‘Where now are your prophets’ expresses the same plural referent permitted by both וְאַיֵּה and ואיו, with no mapped textual note distinguishing them; retain the qere base fallback.
